summary: Double-free or use-after-free may occur in libcurl's HSTS handling when multiple threads process HSTS entries concurrently, leading to memory corruption.

claims.text: Double-free may occur when multiple threads call Curl_hsts_free on the same HSTS entry simultaneously
claims.reasoning: The code in Curl_hsts_parse (lines 213-221) and Curl_hsts (lines 270-275) removes entries from the shared list and frees them via hsts_free without acquiring any lock. When multiple threads share an HSTS cache via CURLOPT_SHARE with CURL_LOCK_DATA_HSTS, the lock callbacks are never invoked by this code, allowing concurrent free of the same entry.

citations.note: hsts_free called immediately after removal, no synchronization visible

claims.text: Use-after-free may occur when other threads access HSTS entries after they have been freed
claims.reasoning: Curl_hsts traverses the list (line 267) and accesses entry fields (lines 270, 276-282) without locking. Another thread could have removed and freed the same entry via the max-age=0 or expiry path, leading to use-after-free.

claims.text: The function Curl_hsts_parse removes HSTS entries without proper synchronization
claims.reasoning: Curl_hsts_parse removes entries when max-age=0 (lines 213-221) without any synchronization primitive. The share mechanism's lock callbacks are not used.

claims.text: The removal of HSTS entries occurs without exclusivity control in multi-threaded context
claims.reasoning: The term 'exclusivity control' maps to the share lock (CURL_LOCK_DATA_HSTS). The code performs lookup, removal, and free without acquiring that lock, so concurrent threads have no exclusion.

claims.text: The code removes entries verbatim without subdomain matching when max-age=0 is received
claims.reasoning: Line 215 passes FALSE as the third argument to Curl_hsts, disabling subdomain matching for the verbatim removal when max-age=0.

key_reasons: Curl_hsts_parse (lines 213-221) and Curl_hsts (lines 270-275) remove and free HSTS entries without acquiring the share lock (CURL_LOCK_DATA_HSTS) that applications register via CURLOPT_SHARE.
The share mechanism expects curl to call the lock/unlock callbacks when accessing shared data; the HSTS code does not, so concurrent threads race on list removal and free.
Double-free and use-after-free are exploitable heap corruption bugs; a malicious server can trigger the max-age=0 or expiry path while other threads traverse the list.
The provided code snippets show no locking in the HSTS implementation. The deterministic checks confirm the quoted lines exist at the target revision.
reply: Thank you for the detailed report and reproduction case. The code in lib/hsts.c (Curl_hsts_parse lines 213-221 and Curl_hsts lines 270-275) removes and frees HSTS entries without acquiring the share lock (CURL_LOCK_DATA_HSTS), so concurrent threads sharing an HSTS cache can double-free or use-after-free. This is a valid thread-safety bug in the HSTS implementation when used with CURLOPT_SHARE. We will investigate the proper locking integration and prepare a fix.
